top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength lattice clock is a separable idea from the frequency comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012). It turns a statistical advantage into an accuracy advantage, moving uncertainty from the 1e-15 range to about 1e-18. It has been reproduced independently at RIKEN, JILA/NIST, PTB and SYRTE and confirmed by intercontinental comparisons. Katori (proposal and first Sr lattice clock) and Ye (accuracy frontier, many-body Fermi-degenerate clock) map onto two identifiable decisive contributions, and the citation is scoped to the lattice clock. No award is the only alternative on the slate and is clearly worse than a mature, verified, distinct achievement.
